case_name: Samineni Appaiah vs Samineni Srinivasa Rao
facts_of_case: Plaintiff filed suit for partition against his father/defendant No.1 and defendants Nos. 2 to 4. Plaintiff claimed he is a coparcener entitled to half share in the property. Defendant No.1 contended that the property was self-acquired and not ancestral.

legal_principles.principle: Illegitimate children do not acquire a right by birth or any interest in the father's estate.
legal_principles.held: They relied upon citation of the Supreme Court reported in GUR NARAIN DAS V/s. GUR TAHAL DAS1 held that 'illegitimate children does not acquire right by birth or any interest in the father's estate and thus they cannot demand for partition during the life time of his father but after his death the illegitimate son succeeds as a coparcener to the separate estate of his father along with legitimate son with a right of survivorship.'
cited_cases: GUR NARAIN DAS V/s. GUR TAHAL DAS1
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to illegitimate children's rights in ancestral properties

legal_principles.principle: Coparcenary property recognises legitimate children only as child gets right in the property by birth.
legal_principles.held: Co-parcenary property recognises legitimate children only as child gets right in the property by birth.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — highlights the importance of legitimacy in coparcenary properties

outcome.final_order: The court set aside the judgment of the trial court and held that the plaintiff is entitled to half share in the property as a coparcener.
